Subject: RFP: SLO evidence packaging + measurement questions

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP. Our procurement and security teams are working through the SLA/SLO questionnaire and have a few follow-ups specific to measurement and evidence packaging before we move to the final evaluation. Could you confirm the following items so we can mark the RFP as "complete" on our side?

1) Evidence bundle: do you provide an off-the-shelf evidence package (logs, aggregated reports, timestamped exports) for SLO claims, or is it produced on demand per audit? Please indicate typical TTL and delivery method.

2) Measurement methodology: we need a short plain-language description of the measurement pipeline (what metrics you compute, sampling rates, how you handle retries/breakdowns, clock sync assumptions, sliding window vs calendar window computation).

3) Maintenance/announced outage handling: how are maintenance windows excluded and how do you communicate them for measurement windows?

4) Service credit example: please provide a worked example showing how you calculate credits when p95/p99 vs uptime thresholds are breached during partial-regional incidents.

5) Telemetry access: do we get a daily telemetry export (raw request-level) or just aggregated metrics? Any constraints on retention or PII redaction we should be aware of?

If you can get us a draft response (even bullets) by end of day Monday (11/22), that will help keep the procurement timeline intact.

Best,

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Draft answers below (high level) and I'm attaching a starter evidence package and our telemetry spec. Happy to expand any section.

1) Evidence bundle
- We provide a standard evidence bundle on request: includes a time-stamped CSV export of aggregated SLO metrics (p50/p95/p99, error-rate, availability) for the requested period, request-level telemetry for the same period (sanitized), and a signed statement of measurement methodology. Typical turnaround for a standard export is 3 business days; expedited (24–48 hours) is available under enterprise support. Delivery is via secure SFTP link or a customer-controlled GCS/Azure container.

2) Measurement methodology (summary)
- Metric definitions: availability is measured as successful inference responses / total requests; latency uses server-side end-to-end processing time (request received -> final token emitted) and is reported as p50/p95/p99 for successful responses only.
- Sampling: default telemetry collects 100% of request metadata and 10% of full payloads for retention efficiency; request-level exports strip/reduce payloads to remove PII unless customer requests otherwise under NDA.
- Aggregation windows: we use 5-minute rolling windows for alerting and a 24-hour lookback with calendar-aligned daily aggregates for SLA reports. SLO compliance is evaluated on calendar-month windows unless otherwise contracted.
- Retries and client-side duplicates: we dedupe by request-id when present; retries that have identical request-ids within a 30s window are collapsed to the last successful attempt for latency accounting.
- Clock sync: all telemetry uses UTC timestamps derived from server epoch; we sync host clocks via NTP to <50ms drift SLA, and exported evidence includes tick alignment metadata.

3) Maintenance / announced outages
- Planned maintenance: customers notify us via their account manager; we publish maintenance windows to the Console and exclude announced windows from SLA calculations if scheduled >72 hours in advance and marked in the maintenance feed. Emergency maintenance is logged and treated as unplanned; we provide post-incident evidence and, where appropriate, credit calculations.

4) Service credit example (worked)
- Suppose monthly uptime SLO = 99.9% for the us-east region. Calendar month has 43,200 minutes. Allowed downtime = 43.2 minutes. If measured downtime (after filtering planned maint) = 130 minutes, excess downtime = 86.8 minutes -> percentage breach = 86.8 / 43,200 = 0.201% over. Service credit = min(max_credit, floor((excess_minutes / total_minutes) * 1000) * $X) per contract.
- For hybrid SLOs (latency p95 threshold), we compute breaches as the number of 5-minute windows where p95 > threshold; crediting is proportional to the fraction of windows breached in the calendar month. Full formula and numerical examples included in Measurement_Examples.pdf.

5) Telemetry access
- Default: daily aggregated exports and a rolling 30-day raw request-level export (sanitized). Enterprise customers can request a longer retention export (90/365 days) via contract. We do not expose raw payloads containing PII by default; PII redaction is performed server-side unless a narrower-scoped NDA is in place.

Attachments: SLO_Telemetry_Spec_v2.xlsx, SLO_Evidence_Package_v1.zip, Measurement_Examples.pdf

Next steps: we'll produce a short one-page "evidence pack" showing the calculation for your most critical window (you flagged Nov 2026 pilot dates) and circulate by EOD Monday. If you need the expedited export, please indicate the delivery target and whether we should include full request payloads under NDA.

Thanks,

Mina — quick internal notes inline.

> - Sampling: default telemetry collects 100% of request metadata and 10% of full payloads for retention efficiency; request-level exports strip/reduce payloads to remove PII unless customer requests otherwise under NDA.

Can we be explicit about sampling uniformity? For audits customers will ask whether sample is uniform across request size, model type, and region. Recommend we say: "sampling is stratified by region and model family to preserve representativeness; we can provide the sampling key in the export."

> - Aggregation windows: we use 5-minute rolling windows for alerting and a 24-hour lookback with calendar-aligned daily aggregates for SLA reports. SLO compliance is evaluated on calendar-month windows unless otherwise contracted.

One more point: call out how partial-region incidents are attributed. We should state that availability is computed per region first, then aggregated by weighted request volume for a global SLA; by default we compute regional SLOs and provide weighted-global if customers request.

> - Clock sync: all telemetry uses UTC timestamps derived from server epoch; we sync host clocks via NTP to <50ms drift SLA, and exported evidence includes tick alignment metadata.

Please add that we provide a clock-drift report for the requested window in the evidence bundle.

I'll add a short worked example of weighted aggregation for the final doc.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Product Manager, Reliability
Redwood Inference

Hi Mina — this is great, thanks. A couple of clarification items before we mark the RFP step complete: 

- For the worked example, can you include a concrete numeric example where a p95 latency breach triggers a credit? We need the math spelled out in dollars for our procurement scoring.
- Confirm the default retention window (30 days) applies to request-level exports and that expanded retention is available under contract (good).
- Important: will the exported request-level telemetry include geo/IPs? If so we need redaction by default for our pilot.
- Does the p99 measurement exclude announced maintenance windows by default, or does that require us to flag windows in the Console?

If you can post the one-page evidence summary and the numeric worked example by COB Monday (11/23), procurement can move this to the approval stage. Also copying Eve from Veritas Audits — will you be able to accept a standard SOC2 audit extract if requested?
